extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or graduate students studying enumerative and algebraic combinatorics / poset theory (readers of Stanley's textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of exercises for Chapter 3 of a combinatorics/textbook on posets: proofs, constructions, enumerations, and examples covering preposets, poset topology, lattices, interval orders, graded posets, binomial/differential posets, and related enumerative problems. Intended as problem set for learning and research practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1: poset and itinerant salespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: [3] What is the connection between a partially ordered set and itinerant salespersons who take revenge on customers who don’t pay their bills?

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 2: preposet → poset canonical map and topology
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [1+] Definitions and construction: Given a preposet (reflexive, transitive relation) form equivalence classes and show resulting quotient is a poset. (b) [1+] Show the canonical map from P to quotient is order-preserving and unique for factorization of order-preserving maps. (c) [2–] Given order-preserving map f:P→Q show unique g making diagram commute. (a)–(d) (next part) For finite preposet define topology P_top from order ideals and show correspondence between finite preposets and finite topologies; characterize when P is a poset (P_top is T0); and order-preserving maps correspond to continuous maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 3: open sets and finite topologies from preposets
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts (a)–(d) (numbering variant) show P_top makes P a finite topological space; given finite topological space X there is unique preposet P with P_top = X; P is a poset iff P_top is T0; maps are order-preserving iff continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4: represent poset by collection of sets (order by inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: [2–] Let P be a poset. Show there exists a collection S of sets partially ordered by inclusion that is isomorphic to P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 5: counting small posets and asymptotics
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2] Draw diagrams of all nonisomorphic posets with 5,6,7 elements and note counts (63,318,2045) and larger counts listed. (b) [5] Let f(n) be number of nonisomorphic n-element posets; find a "reasonable" formula (likely impossible). (c) [5] Statement P: infinitely many values of f(n) are palindromes in base 10 — show P cannot be proved or disproved in ZF set theory. (d) [3] Show log f(n) ∼ (n^2/4) log 2 (or related asymptotic). (e) [3+] Improve (d) to more precise asymptotic with constant C (~0.80587793) and forms for even/odd n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 6: automorphism condition for finite posets
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2] Let P finite and f:P→P order-preserving bijection; show f is an automorphism (i.e., inverse is order-preserving). (b) [2] Show (a) fails for infinite P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 7: chains and maximal chains length properties
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [1+] Give finite poset P where every element is contained in chain of length ℓ (ℓ = longest chain length) yet P has a maximal chain of length less than ℓ. (b) [2] If P finite, no isolated points, longest chain length ℓ, and every cover relation s⋖t lies in some chain of length ℓ, show every maximal chain has length ℓ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 8: self-dual poset without involutive self-duality
rubrics_metrics.description: [3–] Find finite poset P with bijection f:P→P such that s≤t iff f(t)≤f(s) (i.e., P self-dual) but no such bijection satisfying f(f(t))=t for all t (i.e., no involutive self-duality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 9: enumerative true/false about 8-element posets
rubrics_metrics.description: [2–] True or false: the number of nonisomorphic 8-element posets that are not self-dual is 16507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 10: interval poset Int(P) and reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2–]* For posets A,B show Int(A×B*) ≅ Int(A)×Int(B). (b) [2+] If P has 0-hat and Int(P) ≅ Int(Q), show P ≅ A×B and Q ≅ A×B* for some A,B. (c) [3] Find finite P,Q with Int(P)≅Int(Q) but conclusion of (b) fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 11: semiring of isomorphism classes of finite posets
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2] Let A be isomorphism classes of finite posets with + and × from disjoint union and direct product; show A is a commutative semiring. (b) [3–] Adjoin additive inverses to get ring B and characterize B as polynomial ring Z[[P1],[P2],...] on irreducible connected finite posets. (c) [3–] Give irreducible finite posets Pi with factorization counterexamples and explain UFD noncontradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 12: finiteness from chains and antichains
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+] True or false: if every chain and every antichain of poset P is finite, then P is finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 13: antichains finiteness in Jf(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3] If P has every antichain finite, show every antichain of Jf(P) (finitely generated order ideals) is finite. (b) [2] Conversely, give example showing property need not hold for J(P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 14: series-parallel posets and N-free characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2+]* Show finite poset is series-parallel iff it contains no induced Z4 (zigzag of 4). (b) [2+]* For inversion posets Pw of permutations w∈Sn, show Pw is N-free iff w avoids patterns 3142 and 2413 (separable permutations); note enumerative Schröder numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 15: interval orders and semiorders
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–] Show finite poset is interval order iff it is (2+2)-free. (b) [3–] Show finite interval order is a semiorder (unit intervals) iff it is (3+1)-free. (c) [3] Let t(n) count nonisomorphic interval orders; derive generating function formula and initial values. (d) [3] Let u(n) be number of labelled interval orders; give exponential generating function and initial values. (e) [2+] Show number of nonisomorphic n-element interval orders that are series-parallel equals Catalan number Cn. (f) [2]* For given positive lengths ℓ1..ℓn define g(ℓs) as number of labelled interval orders realizable with those lengths; show g equals number of regions of certain hyperplane arrangement; (g) [3] Under linear independence over Q of lengths, define power series z from g and related series y and show differential equation z'/z = y^2, z(0)=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 16: (3+1)-free graded posets enumeration and egf relations
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3] For f(n) = number of graded (3+1)-free partial orders on n labeled elements, show an exponential generating function identity involving G(x) etc. (b) [5] Ask about total number of (3+1)-free posets on an n-element set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 17: constructing posets from collections with trivial automorphism groups
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–] Given collection T of finite posets all with trivial automorphism groups and building posets by replacing elements by antichains, relate egfs F(x) and G(x) with G(x)=F(1−e^{−x}). (b) [2] Compute F,G when T is {chains}. (c) [2+] Show can choose T as interval orders or semiorders with no nontrivial automorphisms; then T generates all nonisomorphic interval orders/semiorders; references to earlier exercises. (d) [3–]* Show number of nonisomorphic n-element graded semiorders equals 1+F_{2n−2} (Fibonacci).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 18: zeros of chain-count polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: [3–] For finite (3+1)-free poset P, let ci be number of i-element chains and define C(P,x)=Σ ci x^i with c0=1; show all zeros of C(P,x) are real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 19: core of a finite poset and dismantlability
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–] Define irreducible element and core(core P) as subposet with no irreducible elements obtained by removing irreducibles; show any two cores are isomorphic. (b) [1+]* If P has 0-hat or 1-hat show core P is single element. (c) [3–] Show core size 1 iff poset of order-preserving maps P→P is connected (dismantlable posets). (d) [5–] Discuss enumeration of nonisomorphic n-element dismantlable posets or labeled versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 20: dimension and embedding in N^d
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2+] Show finite poset P is intersection of d linear orders iff P is isomorphic to a subposet of N^d. (b) For d=2 show equivalence with existence of Q on [n] with s<t or s>t in Q iff s,t incomparable in P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 21: sphere orders question
rubrics_metrics.description: [3+] Define sphere orders: P is sphere order if elements correspond to spheres Si in R^d with nesting determined by order. Prove or disprove every finite poset is a sphere order for some d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 22: determinant formula for poset chains
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+] Given poset P with elements t1..tp regarded as indeterminates, define p×p matrix A with A_{ij}=0 if ti<tj else 1, D=diag(ti), I identity; show det(I+DA) = Σ_C ∏_{ti∈C} ti where sum over all chains C of P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 23: Boolean algebra contains countable and uncountable maximal chains
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+] Show boolean algebra B_P of all subsets of P ordered by inclusion contains both countable and uncountable maximal chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 24: posets with many order ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+] For n≥5 classify (up to isomorphism) n-element posets achieving order-ideal counts 2^n,(3/4)2^n,(5/8)2^n,(9/16)2^n,(17/32)2^n with given multiplicities and show all others have ≤(33/64)2^n order ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 25: lattices among Figure 3.42 posets
rubrics_metrics.description: [2–] Determine which posets in Figure 3.42 are lattices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 26: meet-semilattice with 1 not a lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: [2] Give example of a meet-semilattice with 1-hat (necessarily infinite) that is not a lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 27: recover finite lattice from irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: [3–] For finite lattice L define Irr(L) = {join-irreducible or meet-irreducible elements}. Show L can be uniquely recovered from the poset Irr(L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 28: finite atomic coatomic noncomplemented lattice example
rubrics_metrics.description: [3–] Give example of finite atomic and coatomic lattice that is not complemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 29: maximize meet-irreducibles given number join-irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: [5–] For finite lattice L with n join-irreducibles what is maximal possible number f(n) of meet-irreducible elements?

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 30: obstructions to distributivity and modularity
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2+] Show lattice is distributive iff it contains no sublattice isomorphic to either of two lattices in Figure 3.43. (b) [2+] Show lattice is modular iff it contains no sublattice isomorphic to the first lattice of Figure 3.43.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 31: locally connected posets and distributivity consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2+]* Define locally connected poset (every nonempty open interval is antichain or connected). Show finite locally connected poset with 0-hat and 1-hat is graded. (b) [3] If L finite locally connected lattice with every interval of rank 3 distributive, show L is distributive. (c),(d) Deduce corollaries about products of chains and boolean algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 32: partition into closed intervals and f(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–] For finite graded poset P with 0-hat and rank function ρ define f(P) largest integer d so there is partition into pairwise disjoint closed intervals [s,t] with ρ(t)≥d; find f(B_n) and examples. (b–f) Various identities and bounds for f on products and compositions of posets; compute specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 33: connected poset with given number of chains
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+] Characterize positive integers n for which there exists connected poset with exactly n chains (including empty chain). Empty poset is not connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 34: posets with given F(J(P),x)
rubrics_metrics.description: [2]* Find all nonisomorphic posets P such that F(J(P),x) = (1+x)(1+x^2)(1+x+x^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 35: counts of order ideals by size and generating functions
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2] For fk(n) = number of nonisomorphic n-element posets with exactly k order ideals of each size i=1..n show particular formula for f2(n) = 2^{n−1} etc. (b) [2+] For g(n) a subclass with constraints show g(n)=2^{n−7} for n≥7. (c) [3] Derive generating function identity for f3(n) and g(x) with initial coefficients. (d) [1+] Find fk(n) for k>3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 36: semimodular lattice join-of-atoms subposet geometric
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2] For finite semimodular lattice L let L' be subposet of joins of atoms (including 0); show L' is geometric lattice. (b) [3–] Is L' a sublattice of L?

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 37: supports of vectors in subspace give geometric lattice and application to graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–] Given W subspace of K^n, define L supports of vectors in W ordered by reverse inclusion; show L is geometric lattice. (b) [2+] For graph G show set of spanning subgraphs without isthmus ordered by reverse inclusion is geometric lattice via (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 38: isomorphism between P_k and R_k in distributive lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+] In finite distributive lattice L let P_k be elements that cover k elements and R_k those covered by k; show P_k ≅ R_k and give explicit isomorphism φ in terms of L structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 39: finitary distributive lattices isomorphic to V_t
rubrics_metrics.description: [2+]* Find all finitary distributive lattices L (up to isomorphism) such that L ≅ V_t for some t; if only require locally finite distributive with 0-hat are there other examples?

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 40: size bounds for finite distributive lattices with specified join-irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–] Let L finite distributive of length kr containing k join-irreducibles of rank i for 1≤i≤r (and no others). What is the maximum number of elements L can have; show uniqueness of extreme lattice. (b) [2+] For finitary distributive lattice with exactly two join-irreducibles at each rank show bounds #L_i ≤ F_{i+2} and equality characterization. (c) [5–] If L finitary distributive with infinite antichain t_i of rank i does it follow #L_i ≥ F_{i+2} ?

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 41: repeated Γ operator on functions on finite lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2] For finite lattice L and f:L→N positive at two incomparable elements s,t, define operator Γ_f modifying values at s,t and show for some n we get Γ^n f = Γ^{n+1} f (stabilizes on chain). (b) [3–] Show limiting function independent of choices iff L is distributive. (c) [2+] Characterize limiting ˜f as unique function supported on chain matching cumulative sums over join-irreducibles. (d) [2] Give construction based on ordering join-irreducibles and g(t) cumulative sums. (e) [2] For boolean algebra B_n define f based on excedance sets and show ˜f supported on chain with specified values (connection to permutations/excedances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 42: sublattice Z of Young's lattice and isomorphism to Jf(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2–]* Regard Young's lattice Y of all integer partitions componentwise; let Z be subposet of partitions with odd parts. Show Z is sublattice of Y. (b) [2]* Conclude Z is finitary distributive lattice; determine poset P with Z ≅ Jf(P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 43: product formula for rank-generating function of Jf(Jf(P))
rubrics_metrics.description: [3–] Let P be infinite poset described with elements s_i,t_i and cover relations given; find a nice product formula for rank-generating function F_{Jf(Jf(P))}(q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 44: enumeration of order ideals from permutation word posets
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [3–]* For w=a1...an in S_n define Pw as subposet of [n]×[n] with order by indices with value comparisons; show number of order ideals j(Pw) = n! / ∏ i (i!) where denominator product over multiplicities of letters? (b) [3]* Define Qw variant and show j(Qw) = (n+1)^{n−1}. (note: original block has detailed definitions—exercise asks combinatorial enumeration identities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 45: polynomials L_k(n) counting k-element order ideals in B_n
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2]* Let L_k(n) be number of k-element order ideals of boolean algebra B_n; show for fixed k, L_k(n) is polynomial in n of degree k with leading coefficient 1/k! and integer values; differences ∆^i L_k(0) nonnegative. (b) [3–]* Give explicit polynomials L0..L11(n) and note conjecture about real zeros fails for k=11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 46: sublattices of boolean algebra and egf relations
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) [2]* Let f(n) be number of sublattices of rank n of B_n and show f(n) equals number of partial orders on [n]. (b) [2+]* Let g(n) be number of sublattices of B_n that contain 0-hat and 1-hat; define egfs F(x),G(x) and show G(x)=F(e^{x}−1). (c) [2]* Let h(n) be number of nonempty sublattices of B_n; H(x)=Σ h(n) x^n/n! and show H(x)=e^{2x} G(x).
